vulnerability_analysis: The transferFrom function has a critical logic flaw: when newun == address(0) (initial state), the FIRST transferFrom call with from != address(0) will permanently set newun = to. After this, ALL future transfers to that address are blocked via the require(to != newun) check in both transfer() and transferFrom(). This is a denial-of-service vulnerability that locks a specific address from receiving tokens until the owner manually calls transfernewun().
attack_strategy: 1. Inject tokens to a victim address using deal(). 2. Have the victim approve the attacker to spend their tokens. 3. Call transferFrom(victim, attacker, amount) when newun is still address(0). 4. This triggers the condition that sets newun = attacker, which the oracle verifies (newun != address(0)).
step_by_step_plan: 1. Define TokenBEP20 interface with transferFrom, approve, newun functions. 2. In setUp: instantiate target contract, create victim address, deal tokens to victim, have victim approve attacker. 3. In testExploit: verify newun is initially 0, call transferFrom to trigger the lock, verify newun is now set to non-zero address.
